messages:
Marta Perez: quick mini-sensitivity scan for newmodel-x9b bring-up. ran a small-sample (2k queries) across fp16, int8, and int6. TL;DR: int8 looks like the sweet spot for most traffic; int6 saves more cost but has a measurable drop on multi-turn QA. details below.

Jonathan Lee: nice — can you drop the key numbers?

Marta Perez: sure. summary: 
- cost per 1k tokens: fp16=$0.82, int8=$0.64 (-22%), int6=$0.53 (-17% vs int8, -35% vs fp16)
- QA F1 (closed-book, multi-turn dev slice): fp16=86.2, int8=85.5 (-0.7), int6=83.2 (-3.0)
- Inference p95 latency (seq len 512, gtx-optim): fp16=210ms, int8=170ms, int6=150ms
- Prefix/KV cache hit sensitivity: short queries (>60% cache hits) show negligible F1 delta for int6; long-context chains drop steeply

Kevin Ng: where did hallucination metrics go? any rise in hallucination rate for int6?

Marta Perez: good call. hallucination (extrinsic factuality test): fp16=4.1% errors, int8=4.5% (+0.4), int6=6.8% (+2.7). most of the extra errors are on long multi-step retrieval+compose cases.

Sara Kovacs: so product impact: if GTN wants to switch, we should probably route short one-shot queries to int6 and keep long chains on int8/fp16. can we express that as a routing rule?

Marta Perez: yep. proposed routing snippet for redwood routes: 
```json
{
  "rules": [
    {"id":"short_queries_int6","if":"tokens<=64 and kv_cache_hit>=0.5","route":"newmodel-x9b-int6"},
    {"id":"default","route":"newmodel-x9b-int8"},
    {"id":"fallback","route":"newmodel-x9b-fp16","if":"latency_slo_violated"}
  ]
}
```

Jonathan Lee: what about traffic split for a conservative rollout? 5% holdback? 1%?

Marta Perez: my suggestion: 3-stage rollout: 1) canary 1% traffic int6 short-rule enabled but gated by quality monitor. 2) expand to 10% for short-query heavy products if eval signals stable. 3) cross-traffic hybrid at 30% with auto rollback on quality regressions >1.5% absolute on the primary GTN metric.

eval-bot: smoke run results uploaded: https://internal.redwood/evals/1776590000 — quick digest: int6 pass rate on micro-sanity: 78/100; int8: 92/100; fp16: 95/100.

Kevin Ng: thanks. any particular prompt families that blow up on int6?

Marta Perez: yes — priming-heavy workflows (few-shot with large context + chain-of-thought) and retrieval-augmented multi-step edits. short summarization and classification slices are fine.

Sara Kovacs: product ask: can we quantify unit-econ win per 100M tokens if we move 40% short-query traffic to int6? quick estimate pls.

Marta Perez: rough calc: baseline mix cost (current mostly fp16) avg $0.72/k; shifting 40% of short queries to int6 lowers blended to ~$0.59/k -> ~18% cost reduction. For 100M tokens that's ~$11.4k savings/month. caveat: excludes infra fixed costs and potential incident remediation from regressions.

Jonathan Lee: sounds reasonable. next steps?

Marta Perez: action items: 
1) set up 1% canary with the short-query rule tomorrow (eng-platform)
2) add an automated eval gate (eval team) that runs 5k synthetic checks every hour and fires if primary metric drops >1.0%
3) product to confirm which user flows are eligible for short-query routing (Sara)
4) ops to prepare rollback runbook for hallucination spikes (Kevin)

Kevin Ng: I'll draft the runbook. watchlist: support tickets, hallucination alarms, latency p95.

Sara Kovacs: I'll send product whitelist by EOD. +1 on the 1% canary.

Marta Perez: cool. tagging folks: @eng-platform for routing rollout and @eval-team for gate. thanks all :thumbsup:

eval-bot: reminder scheduled: daily eval summary at 08:00 UTC.
